5-6 quart crock pot- Buy 3 pounds of quality (not from Aldi) marbled chuck roast when it is on sale (chuck roast is the best kind for a crock pot). Go to Aldi and buy a bag of potatoes, a bag of onions and a bag of carrots for a total of $3-4.00.

Cut the roast in to 3-5 hunks. Clean but don't peel the potatoes, then cut them into 2-3 inch pieces.Clean but don't peel carrots, then break them in to 4 inch pieces. Peel off out layer of onions and quarter/eighth them. Put the potatoes on the bottom, then put the meat in, add in the carrots in, put the onions around and on top of the meat.

Some people use/buy/have some type of broth, but I think a 1cup of two of water is fine to dump in to get it all cooking... cook on low for 8-10 hours... or however long you want until you can stick a fork in the meat, twist and it separates easy.

Double check all of that online, but it is too simple to do and kind of hard to mess up. Pre-spice the meat as you desire, I use salt and pepper.

The main point is Chuck roast is the best for this recipe. Last week it was on sale for $4.99 at the quality meat place and I made this recipe. If you don't have an Aldi, then buy the veggies where ever, but if you do have an Aldi do not be so uppity to think it is an only for poor people store. I DO NOT buy most things there (like I DO NOT buy meat at Aldi), but I DO buy eggs, milk, potatoes, onions, saltine crackers and stuff like because it is damn near 30% the price of the regular grocery store. I used to be "too good" to go to Aldi, but a couple of years ago I was helping an old guy (who had tons of money) but couldn't get around as well as he used to, so when he needed some help and I donated my time and would drive him around to wherever to buy groceries, meds, hair cut etc... and he said "lets go to Aldi". I did not question it or comment (I respect old guys)... and I was not, am not, impressed with the ugly store and boxes on shelves, but I am impressed with the prices. They have some inexpensive items that taste fine.

TL/DR I shouldn't offer any recipes for advice for this, because if I did, I would probably go on and on and on and then go off topic. SO anyway... now I'm hungry again. BonAppetite
